newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Gunmen kill three in Karachi, including KESC chief.
newsitem.headline: Gunmen kill three in Karachi, including KESC chief.

text.p: Gunmen killed the head of Karachi Electric Supply Corporation (KESC), his driver and guard on Saturday, police said.
They said two assailants in a car attacked KESC managing director Shahid Hamid's vehicle in the southern Defence Housing Society area of Karachi as he was driving to his office.
Earlier reports said the attackers had been on a motorcycle.
Hamid, 46, and his driver were killed on the spot, while the guard died in hospital.
There was no claim of responsibility for the attack and no immediate word on its motive.
A KESC spokesman said many groups were "after Hamid", but declined to elaborate.
Hamid took charge of KESC on December 10, vowing to cut its losses, improve its service and prepare it for privatisation.
The KESC has come under harsh fire from ordinary people and various lobbies over for the last few months due to long and frequent power cuts in residential and industrial areas.
These grievances have occasionally spilt into violence when angry citizens attacked KESC offices and employees.
In a separate overnight shooting in the Defence Housing area, police said armed robbers killed a policeman and wounded two when the policemen tried to stop their vehicle.
More than 150 people have been killed in political violence in the southern port of Karachi in the past four months, police say.
